  <h1 style="font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 10px;">Dennis Nientimp</h1>
  <p style="font-size: 1.2em; max-width: 600px; margin: 0 auto;">
    Interdisciplinary social scientist and musician.
    
    
    I have a background in psychology, behavioral sciences and sociology. In my PhD I researched participation in community energy  through a combination of social network analysis, computational methods and participatory modelling. Recently I applpied Agent Based Modelling and empirically informed Diffusion Models to derive testable hypothesis about the mechanisms that drive the adoption of sustainable practices and aid CEI in develeoping mobilization strategies. I applied such insights in co-creation projects, in which stakeholders act as co-researcher and we collaboratively develop CEI dissemination strategiies. 
    
    In the past I researched social interactions with and perceptions of robots at the Behavior Science institute in Nijmegen and I investigated behavior change interventions to promote sustainable food choices at the institute for Environmental Psychology in Vienna. In my bachelors I delved into computational linguistics, studying how kinematic movements support verbal communication, at the Max Plank institute for linguistics in Nijmegen. 
    
    That said I have broad interest in social scientific topics and beyond and I am eager to learn new methodology. Here a few keywords describing my current reseqrch interest: social network analysis; simualtions; diffusion of innovations; energy transition; networks and sustainability; ABM; behavior change; collective action; HRI
    
    
  </p>
